title: `generate` and `watch` delete previous output and the breaking-change lock before validating; breaking-change gate (--strict/--force/prompt) is dead
trigger_reproducer: (a) generate OK, append `garbage {{{` to a .veld file, run `veld generate` -> exit 1 and `generated/`, `veld/generated`, `.veld.lock.json`, `.veld-cache.json` all gone. (b) generate OK, remove `action GetUser`, run `veld generate --strict` -> exit 0, no breaking-change report; same with --force and plain. `veld ci --strict` on the identical state exits 1 with "action GetUser removed" (ci does not call runClean).
expected_vs_actual: expected a failed/invalid generation to leave prior output intact and `--strict` to block breaking changes (documented CI gate). Actual: `runClean(rc)` (RemoveAll of every output dir plus `diff.DeleteLock`) runs at generate.go:759 before `computePreChanges` (generate.go:1021), so the lock baseline is already deleted and `HasBreaking` is always false; and any parse/validate/unknown-backend error leaves the user with an empty output dir. watch.go:56 does the same on start and so also loses lock/diff.
impact: CI breaking-change protection advertised in CLAUDE.md does not work for `veld generate`; any typo wipes generated code that the developer's own non-generated files import; the interactive prompt (`promptContinue`) is unreachable.
root_cause: ordering - clean precedes parse/validate/diff; lock deletion is bundled into runClean.
recommendation: refactor - parse+validate+diff first, emit into a temp dir, swap on success, and stop deleting the lock in runClean.
regression_check: test that a failing generate preserves out dir and lock; test `generate --strict` exits 1 when an action is removed.

title: `--out`/`out` validation accepts the directory containing the contract sources; `generate` then deletes them
trigger_reproducer: project `proj/veld/{veld.config.json,app.veld,...}`; run `veld generate --out=../veld` (in `proj/`). validateOutPath only rejects basenames `..`, `.`, `/`, `\`. `../veld` resolves to the config dir; runClean `os.RemoveAll` deleted the entire `veld/` tree (sources + config), then failed `reading ...app.veld`.
expected_vs_actual: expected refusal when the output dir contains/equals the config dir, the input file's dir, cwd, or a parent of any of them. Actual: accepted and wiped. Also accepted: `--out=C:\Users\x`, any absolute path.
impact: irrecoverable loss of the user's contract files from one mis-typed flag or config value; same path is hit by `veld clean` and by workspace entries (not validated at all).
root_cause: shallow lexical basename check; RemoveAll with no containment, marker-file, or ownership check.
recommendation: fix - refuse any out dir that is, contains, or is contained by config dir / input dir / cwd / home / drive root, and only delete dirs carrying a `.veld-generated` marker.
regression_check: tests for out=configDir, out=parent-of-configDir, out=inputDir, workspace entry out=".".

title: `veld clean` / pre-generate clean recursively delete any directory `out` points at (e.g. `src`)
trigger_reproducer: config `{"out":"./src"}`, `src/business.ts` present, `veld clean` -> prints "Cleaned ...\src", exit 0, `src/` is gone including the user file. No prompt, no manifest, no `--yes`.
expected_vs_actual: only files Veld generated should be removed (CLAUDE.md: "Veld never touches developer business logic"). Actual: whole directory.
impact: data loss for projects that mix generated and handwritten code in one folder (Veld's own docs allow `out` anywhere).
root_cause: no generated-file manifest or marker; `os.RemoveAll(dir)`.
recommendation: refactor - write a manifest (or `.veld-generated` marker) and delete only manifest files (plus empty dirs); refuse to clean unmarked non-empty dirs without `--force`.
regression_check: clean on a dir with foreign files leaves them; clean on an unmarked dir refuses.

title: `veld init` overwrites existing README.md and veld/*.veld files when no config exists
trigger_reproducer: directory with `README.md` ("MY README") and `veld/app.veld` ("// mine") but no veld.config.json; `veld init` exit 0 -> README.md now "# My Veld Project", app.veld replaced by scaffold.
expected_vs_actual: CLAUDE.md "veld init never overwrites files"; the guard only checks for config files, then `os.WriteFile` unconditionally.
impact: silent loss of a project README and any pre-existing contract files.
root_cause: existence check limited to two config paths; no per-file check.
recommendation: fix - skip or abort on any existing target path (O_EXCL).
regression_check: init in dir with README.md leaves it byte-identical.

title: Go backend (plain `net/http` strategy) generates code that does not compile
trigger_reproducer: `examples/go-svelte` copy: `veld generate` then `cd generated && go vet ./...` -> `internal\routes\todos.go:14:2: undefined: mux` (9 uses). The function parameter is named `r *http.ServeMux` but the body calls `mux.HandleFunc`.
expected_vs_actual: compiles; actual: build failure for the default Go backend.
impact: Go backend unusable out of the box.
root_cause: param name vs variable name mismatch in the plain strategy template.
recommendation: fix - emit consistent receiver name; add compile test.
regression_check: go build of generated output in CI (F-CLI-18).

title: Python backend routes contain a SyntaxError for actions with input
trigger_reproducer: `examples/python-vue` copy: `veld generate` (default config, no validate flag) then `python -I -m compileall generated` -> `input = CreateTodoInputSchema(**body = data  # CreateTodoInputSchema).model_dump()` SyntaxError (also users_routes.py:40).
expected_vs_actual: valid Python; actual: syntax error, module cannot import.

recommendation: fix - repair the template and add py_compile test.

title: `import @alias/*` and `@alias/**` are lexed as a block comment and silently delete the rest of the file
location: internal/lexer/lexer.go:240-251 and :253-257 (comment detection precedes the path-token branch at :315); parser consumer internal/parser/parser.go:210-215
trigger_reproducer: `fe-audit/cases/66-wildcard-comment-swallow/main.veld` containing `import @models/*` followed by `model Foo {...}` and `module M {...}`; run `veld.exe validate main.veld` and `veld.exe ast main.veld`. Also the shipped example `examples/microservices/veld/app.veld` (`import @services/**`): `veld ast veld/app.veld` returns `"models": null, "modules": null`.
expected_vs_actual: Expected the wildcard import to load all files in `models/` and keep the remainder of the file. Actual: the `/*` after `@models` opens a block comment that runs to the next `*/` or EOF; `Foo` and `M` vanish, validation prints "Contract is valid". The documented forms in docs/architecture/overview.md:55 and docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md:189 (`import @models/*`) are the broken ones; `import /models/*` and `from @models import *` work.
impact: silent loss of models/modules, generated code missing endpoints with no diagnostic.
root_cause: `/` followed by `*` is tested for comment start before the lexer knows it is inside an import path; `//` in paths has the same problem (`path: //x`, extra case e19).
recommendation: fix, make comment recognition context-aware (or lex `@alias/…` import paths as one token) and add an "unterminated block comment" error.
regression_check: loader test with `import @models/*` + model afterwards asserting model count; lexer test that `@a/*` and `@a/**` yield TPath; microservices example must yield non-empty AST.

title: `veld generate` deletes the lock file and output before the breaking-change gate, so breaking-change detection never fires (and an invalid contract wipes the previous output)
location: cmd/veld/generate.go:758-760 (`runClean`), gate at :1019-1035, `computePreChanges` :1126-1140, `runClean` removing the lock at :51; same ordering in cmd/veld/watch.go:56
trigger_reproducer: project in `fe-audit/gate/`: `veld generate` once with a model `A{x:int,y:string}` and `POST /a`; then change to `A{x:int}` and `PUT /b` (field removed, method and path changed) and run `veld generate --strict`. Exit code 0, no breaking-change output; `.veld.lock.json` was deleted by `runClean` before `computePreChanges` read it. Second repro: put `model A extends A {}`; `veld generate` fails validation but `generated/`, `.veld.lock.json`, `.veld-cache.json` are already gone.
expected_vs_actual: CLAUDE.md says "pre-emit gate: interactive prompt by default, `--strict` exits 1 (CI), `--force` skips prompt". Actual: gate input (`LoadLock`) is always empty for a non-dry-run, non-incremental generate; `--strict` can never fail.
impact: the CI safety feature advertised as a differentiator is a no-op; developers lose their previous generated output when the contract has any error.
root_cause: `runClean(rc)` unconditionally precedes the gate and also deletes the lock (generate.go:51), and runs before parse/validate.
recommendation: fix, validate first, run the gate against the lock, only then clean/emit; never delete the lock in generate.
regression_check: CLI test: generate, introduce each breaking change, assert `generate --strict` exits non-zero and leaves output intact; test that a validation failure leaves `generated/` untouched.

title: Generated output is not deterministic: types/index.ts export order varies between runs
location: internal/emitter/tsshared/types.go:442 (range over map `claimed` builds moduleExports unsorted)
trigger_reproducer: veld init; run `veld generate` six times; sha256 of the tree: run 3 differed in types/index.ts (lead reviewer); docs track saw 4 distinct hashes in 6 runs
expected_vs_actual: Expected identical output; actual export order changes

recommendation: fix - sort moduleExports; add a determinism test over every emitter
regression_check: generate twice on every fixture and byte-compare (CI)

title: Hyphenated header names are emitted as identifiers in every language, producing uncompilable output
location: internal/parser/parser.go:961 (synthetic `<Action>Headers` model); consumers: python models/items.py:218, go internal/models/items.go:184, java CreateItemHeaders.java:8, csharp CreateItemHeaders.cs, php CreateItemHeaders.php:12, rust models/items.rs:211, node-js types/items.js:141, dart/kotlin/swift clients, graphql, prisma, sql
trigger_reproducer: `headers: { "Idempotency-Key": string }` (the form shown in CLAUDE.md contract syntax). `veld generate --backend=python --backend-framework=flask --validate` then `python -m compileall out/pyflask` -> SyntaxError. Same via go build, javac, node --check, graphql buildSchema.
expected_vs_actual: valid identifier (`idempotency_key`) with wire name kept in a string literal vs `idempotency-_key` / `Idempotency-key`.

recommendation: fix -- sanitise header field names once in the parser (keep original as wire name) and have emitters use the wire name only in string literals.
regression_check: compile-of-generated-code CI job per language with a contract containing a hyphenated header.

title: Emitter unit tests assert substrings; generated output is never compiled, so most non-Node backends ship uncompilable code with a green suite
location: internal/emitter/backend/*/*_test.go (e.g. rust/rust_test.go:160 asserts `pub fn router<S>() -> impl std::any::Any`)
trigger_reproducer: `go test ./internal/emitter/...` passes; building generated output fails (see run log).
expected_vs_actual: tests should fail when output does not compile; they enshrine broken stubs.

title: Default Python backend (no --validate) emits a syntax-error route file and no route registration
trigger_reproducer: `veld generate --backend=python --frontend=none`; compileall -> `input = CreateItemSchema(**body = data  # CreateItemSchema).model_dump()`.
expected_vs_actual: Pydantic-validated route calling the service and registered with Flask vs syntax error, missing `from flask import request`, missing schemas module (not emitted), `# register:` comment instead of add_url_rule, `raise RuntimeError(body)` instead of returning a response.
impact: the primary documented Python flow (CLAUDE.md "Pydantic validation") produces nothing runnable; only `--backend-framework=flask --validate` works (after F-MULTI-01/04 are fixed).
root_cause: a strategy placeholder (ExtractBody) is interpolated as code; the Pydantic schema emitter named in python.go's header no longer exists.
recommendation: rewrite -- make Flask the default strategy and always emit the zero-dependency validators; drop Pydantic claims.
regression_check: compileall + import + run Flask smoke test for default flags.

title: Go routes do not compile (`mux` undefined) and run without input validation or query/header binding
trigger_reproducer: `go build ./...` in out/go -> `internal/routes/items.go:14:2: undefined: mux` (after the F-MULTI-01 rename). After patching: `{}` body -> 201; role "bogus" accepted; GetItem receives nil query; CreateItem receives nil headers; date field "2020-01-01" fails to decode.

root_cause: strategy emits `mux.` while the function parameter is named `r`; no validation emitter for Go.
recommendation: fix -- name the param consistently, add generated Validate() methods, bind query/headers, map date to a date-aware type.
regression_check: go build + vet of generated output; httptest-based smoke test.

title: `veld generate` deletes the whole output directory (including user files) before every run
location: cmd/veld/generate.go:40-50 (runClean), 757-760 (call); comment at 141-142 claims the opposite
trigger_reproducer: put my-notes.ts, usersub/a.txt, routes/stale.routes.ts in the out dir; `veld generate --force --out=./o1`. All gone.
expected_vs_actual: "user files are never touched; use `veld clean`" vs `os.RemoveAll(outDir)` on every non-dry-run generate (also workspace and watch).
impact: hand-added files, node_modules, co-located code in the out dir are lost; all mtimes reset, defeating tsc/vite incremental caches.
root_cause: runClean invoked unconditionally; no manifest of generated files.
recommendation: refactor: write a manifest of emitted files and delete only stale manifest entries, never RemoveAll.
regression_check: foreign file in out dir survives two generates; a removed module's file is deleted.

title: `--out` pointing at the project/source directory deletes the contract and sources
trigger_reproducer: sandbox sb/proj containing app.veld and notes.txt: `veld generate --input=app.veld --out=../proj`. On Windows RemoveAll partially failed (cwd in use) but app.veld and notes.txt were deleted, then the run errored "reading app.veld". Unix would remove everything. `--out=.`/`..` are refused. Root (`/`) deliberately not tested.
expected_vs_actual: refuse an out dir that contains the input, config, cwd or a filesystem root vs lexical check only.
impact: irreversible deletion of the user's source of truth; with F-NODE-01 any `--out=src` wipes code.
root_cause: textual validation; recursive clean.
recommendation: fix: resolve to absolute and refuse if out is an ancestor-or-equal of cwd/config dir/input file or a root; fix F-NODE-01.

title: A failing generate leaves the previous output deleted; watch does this on every save
trigger_reproducer: generate OK, append garbage to the contract, regenerate: parse error printed and the out dir no longer exists. In `veld watch`, saving a half-edited contract wipes generated code (debounce is 300ms; errors are printed and the loop continues, which is good), breaking the dev server until the contract is valid again.
expected_vs_actual: failed run is a no-op vs destructive.
impact: dev-loop breakage; CI leaves an empty out dir after a failure.
root_cause: clean precedes parse; no staging directory.
recommendation: refactor: emit to a temp dir and swap on success only.
regression_check: broken contract leaves previous output byte-identical.

title: Breaking-change gate and `--strict` never fire (lock deleted before the diff)
trigger_reproducer: generate; remove action DeleteItem; `veld generate --strict` -> exit 0, nothing reported; lock re-saved without the action.
expected_vs_actual: exit 1 with breaking changes (CLAUDE.md "Contract Safety Features") vs silent success.
impact: the advertised CI protection is non-functional.
root_cause: runClean removes .veld.lock.json and .veld-cache.json ahead of the diff.
recommendation: fix: stop deleting the lock in generate/watch.
regression_check: end-to-end: remove an action, run `generate --strict`, expect exit 1.

title: Static routes shadowed by earlier parametric routes (including middleware-protected ones)
trigger_reproducer: `GET /items/:id` declared before `GET /items/boom`, `/items/guarded` (middleware AuthGuard), `/items/old`. Requests to each are answered by getItem; authGuard never invoked.
expected_vs_actual: each action reached by its own handler vs later same-method static paths unreachable and answered by another action without the middleware.
impact: dead endpoints; protected action silently replaced by an unprotected one.
root_cause: no specificity ordering and no validator/lint rule for overlapping routes (lint duplicate-route does not catch it).
recommendation: fix: emit static-segment routes before parametric ones per method and add a validator error for ambiguous overlap.
regression_check: `/:id` then `/me` reaches the right handler under express.

title: Generated output does not compile under `tsc --strict`
location: frontend/typescript/client.go (`query as Record<string, unknown>`, `extraHeaders: Record<string,string>`), backend/node/routes.go (headers object literal)
trigger_reproducer: any contract with a `query:` model or `headers:` block; `tsc --noEmit --strict` (errors in section 1 step 5). Every framework wrapper inherits them.
expected_vs_actual: clean compile vs 4 errors (5 with --validate).
impact: users must disable strict or edit generated files.
root_cause: models are classes with methods, so literals/instances are not assignable to or from Record types; no test compiles the output.
recommendation: fix: emit plain interfaces (or cast via unknown) and add a tsc compile test.
regression_check: CI generates the rich contract and runs tsc --strict --noEmit.

title: 2FA bypass - the pre-TOTP "partial" JWT is a fully valid session token
exploitability: anyone who knows a victim's password (the exact attacker TOTP exists to stop); no other precondition. Also usable by a stolen password from a leaked DB of another service.
location: internal/server/handlers/auth.go:105-117 (partial issued with `IssueJWT`), internal/server/auth/token.go:56-92 (no purpose claim), internal/server/auth/middleware.go:70-100 (accepts any valid JWT as a session)
trigger_reproducer: `e2e-run2.log` E7. alice enables TOTP; `POST /auth/login` returns `{"partial":"eyJ...","totp_required":true}`; `GET /auth/me` with `Authorization: Bearer <partial>` -> `HTTP 200 {... "totp_enabled":true}`; `POST /tokens` with the partial -> HTTP 201 (admin API token minted). Never supplied a TOTP code.
expected_vs_actual: partial token should only be accepted by /auth/totp-login; actual: accepted everywhere for 5 minutes, and it can mint a permanent admin API token.
impact: two-factor authentication gives no protection at all against password compromise; attacker gets a durable `vtk_` token.
root_cause: `JWTClaims` has only sub/exp/iat; the partial and the full token are indistinguishable.
recommendation: fix - add a `typ`/`purpose` claim (e.g. "2fa-pending") that `resolveAuth` rejects, and require it in totp-login.
regression_check: test that a partial token gets 401 on /auth/me, /tokens, /packages (POST).

title: Storage path traversal on publish - arbitrary `*.tar.gz` write, overwrite and delete
exploitability: any registered user (registration and org creation are open and unverified); becomes owner of their own org, which is the only precondition for Publish.
location: internal/server/handlers/packages.go:122,177 (unvalidated `manifest.name`/`version` into the key); internal/server/storage/storage.go:33-36 (`Clean` then `Join` with no containment check); packages.go:217 and :334 (Delete of the same key)
trigger_reproducer: `e2e-run1.log` E4. Publish `{"org":"mal9041","name":"../../traversal-9041","version":"1.0.0"}` -> 201; file created at `<scratch>\reg-audit\traversal-9041\1.0.0.tar.gz`, i.e. outside the storage root. Then publish `name="../acme9041/auth"` -> victim's `acme9041/auth/1.0.0.tar.gz` overwritten (disk sha changed from 53da33... to d94982...; victim download shows header sha 53da33... but body sha d94982...). Then mallory `DELETE /packages/mal9041/..%2Facme9041%2Fauth/1.0.0` -> 204 and victim's tarball is gone (`HTTP 404 file not found in storage`).
expected_vs_actual: name/version must be constrained and the key must stay under the root; actual: arbitrary relative key. Content is attacker-controlled bytes; suffix is always `.tar.gz` (limits it to overwriting/creating `*.tar.gz` files anywhere the server user can write, and deleting such files). It breaks other orgs' packages (integrity-check failure at best; if the victim version's DB sha were also attacker-controlled it would be a substitution) and can destroy any `*.tar.gz` on the host.
impact: cross-tenant integrity/availability damage; arbitrary file write/delete of `.tar.gz` outside the data dir; combined with the missing sha anchoring on the client (F-REG-09) a path to serving wrong content.
root_cause: no validation of package name/version (no charset, length, semver); trust in `filepath.Clean`.
recommendation: fix - validate org/name (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`) and strict semver at the handler, derive the storage key from the DB ids (content-addressed by sha), and verify `filepath.Rel(root, p)` stays inside.
regression_check: publish with `..`, `/`, `%2F`, NUL, backslash, very long, and unicode names -> 400; assert nothing outside root.

title: Token scope model is not enforced; a read-only token can mint admin tokens and delete versions
exploitability: holder of any valid API token (e.g. a leaked read-only CI token).
location: internal/server/handlers/auth.go:393-439 (CreateToken: no scope check, scopes/org_id accepted verbatim); handlers/packages.go:276-338 (Deprecate/Delete never call `HasScope`); only packages.go:105 checks `write`; middleware.go:57-68 (`HasScope` returns true for JWT); `read` scope never checked; `org_id` of a token never enforced
trigger_reproducer: E2/E3. `ro` token (scopes [read]) -> `POST /tokens` with `scopes:[read,write,delete,admin]` -> token returned. Publish with `ro` -> 403 "missing 'write' scope", but with the minted token -> 201. `DELETE /packages/acme/auth/0.9.0` with the read-only token -> 204.
expected_vs_actual: scopes limit what a token can do; actual: trivially bypassed.
impact: least-privilege CI tokens give no protection; a leak of a "read" token is a full account compromise (publish, delete, rotate).
root_cause: scopes bolted on at one handler; token management reachable with token auth.
recommendation: fix - require JWT session (or `admin` scope) for token management, validate scope enum, check scopes centrally in middleware per route, enforce `org_id`.
regression_check: matrix test of (scope x endpoint).

title: Client integrity check is optional and self-referential; http registries are accepted without warning
exploitability: network attacker on any `http://` registry URL; malicious or compromised registry operator; anyone able to alter response headers (misconfigured proxy/CDN).
location: internal/registry/client.go:208-210 (sha taken from the same response; copy error ignored), cmd/veld/registry.go:232-236 (`if remoteSHA != ""`), 37-60 (no scheme check on login), credentials.go:230 (token sent over whatever scheme)
trigger_reproducer: MITM proxies in section 4: stripping `X-Veld-SHA256` -> `Pulled`, malicious `veld.config.json` with `postGenerate` hook written; replacing body and header consistently -> `Pulled`. `veld registry login --registry http://localhost:18080` accepted, token stored and sent in cleartext (CLAUDE.md and help text show http examples; `ftp://` is rejected only by Go's transport).
expected_vs_actual: fail closed when the sha is absent; authenticity anchored out of band (lockfile/signature) and https required for non-loopback hosts; actual: all optional.
impact: tampered contracts flow straight into code generation (`.veld` models drive generated code; a pulled `veld.config.json` can carry a `postGenerate` command that runs on the next `veld generate` if it ends up as the project config, see F-REG-20). Tokens and packages travel in plaintext if the operator uses http.
root_cause: checksum is transport-corruption detection, not a trust root.
recommendation: fix - require header (fail closed), refuse non-https except loopback unless `--insecure`, add a `veld.lock` with pinned sha256, and plan package signing.
regression_check: pull against a server omitting the header must fail; login to `http://example.com` must fail.

title: Unpack has no limits, writes in place, and drops I/O errors
exploitability: malicious package author (any registered user can publish a public package; archive content is never validated server-side) or malicious registry; victim = anyone who runs `veld registry pull`.
trigger_reproducer: section 2 table: 1.24 MiB -> 1 GiB file in 2.9 s; 1.4 MB -> 100,000 files in 4 min; partial extraction left behind; truncated file left; `MkdirAll`/`io.Copy`/`Close` errors dropped (tarball.go:130,134,139,140).
expected_vs_actual: cap entries (count, per-file, total), reject non-regular entries explicitly, extract to a temp dir and rename atomically, check all errors; actual: none.
impact: disk-fill/CPU denial of service on developer or CI machines; corrupt half-extracted contracts used silently; symlink-safety only by accident (item 2); stale files persist across versions.
root_cause: minimal implementation.
recommendation: rewrite - small hardened extractor (regular files and dirs only, `LimitReader`, count/size caps, containment via `filepath.Rel`, temp dir + rename) shared by CLI and server validation.
regression_check: the section 2 corpus as a test table.

title: Stored XSS sinks in the web UI (usernames, org text, versions, deprecation text)
evidence_status: source-supported defect (hostile values stored and returned by the API - reproduced; rendering in a browser not executed)
exploitability: any registered user (username, org description/display_name, token names) and any publisher (version string, package name; version string is not validated). Victim = any visitor/member viewing the page.
location: internal/server/web/index.html:335 (`${u.username}`), 377 (`${e.message}`), 420, 456-457, 486-492, 519-524 (`v.version`, `v.deprecated`), 543-544, 564-565, 585-587 (`m.username`, `m.email`, inline `onclick="removeMember('${org.name}','${m.username}')"`), 616, 633-634; only `escHtml` uses are lines 497, 503; no CSP.
trigger_reproducer: E1/E12: org description `` stored (psql shows it verbatim); username `` registered with 201; version `
expected_vs_actual: output-encode every interpolation; actual: template literals into `innerHTML`.
impact: script runs same-origin as the victim; the HttpOnly cookie is not readable but the script can call the API as the victim (mint admin API tokens, publish, delete, change org roles) and read the minted token back.

recommendation: rewrite - render via `textContent`/a small escaping template tag or a framework, add a strict CSP, and validate username/org/package/version charsets server-side.

title: Concurrent/duplicate publish deletes the published tarball (DB row left pointing at nothing)
exploitability: any org owner/admin (or two honest CI jobs racing).
location: packages.go:162-166 (check-then-act), 177-200 (Put renames over the existing key), 216-218 (on unique-violation: `Storage.Delete(tarballKey)` removes the winner's file)
trigger_reproducer: E5. Two concurrent publishes of the same new version: in 10/25 (run 1) and 16/25 (run 2) iterations one got 201, the other 500, and the subsequent download returned `HTTP 404 file not found in storage` although the DB row exists and `GET /versions` lists it.
expected_vs_actual: loser gets 409 and the winner's artifact is intact; actual: published version silently corrupted/unavailable.
impact: data loss of a "published, immutable" artifact; also leaves a pkg row created before the tarball is validated (name squatting with zero versions).
root_cause: file written under its final key before the DB uniqueness decision; unconditional delete in the error path.
recommendation: fix - write to a unique temp key, insert row inside a transaction, then `link`/rename only on success (or content-address blobs by sha).
regression_check: parallel-publish test (N=20) asserts exactly one 201 and a downloadable artifact.

title: Versions are not immutable and "latest" is not the highest semver
exploitability: org owner (delete + republish); a malicious/compromised owner or stolen write+delete token.
location: packages.go:311-338 (hard delete), 162 (only existing rows block); db.go:~470 (`ORDER BY published_at DESC`), cmd/veld/registry.go:199-209 (`versions[0]`), models.go:ParseSemver (unused by the CLI, tolerant parsing)
trigger_reproducer: E3. Deleted 0.9.0 and republished 0.9.0 with different content -> 201 (new sha). Published 2.0.0 then 1.0.1: list order `[1.0.1 2.0.0 0.9.0 1.0.0]`, so `veld registry pull @acme/auth` resolves to 1.0.1. Deprecated versions are also eligible for "latest".
expected_vs_actual: npm/crates semantics (a version, once published, is never reusable; latest = highest non-prerelease); actual: pinned versions can change content; "latest" is "most recently published".
impact: supply-chain integrity: consumers who pinned `@org/pkg@1.0.0` get different bytes after delete+republish, and no consumer-side lock/sha exists to notice. No semver ranges are supported (only exact or latest).
root_cause: no tombstones, no semver validation, ordering by timestamp.
recommendation: fix - tombstone deleted versions (name+version permanently reserved), validate semver on publish, compute latest by semver, record sha in a consumer lockfile.
regression_check: delete-then-republish must 409; ordering test.

title: No rate limiting, lockout, or TOTP replay protection
exploitability: anonymous.
location: server.go:59 (no limiter in the handler chain); auth.go:88-159; totp.go:28-38
trigger_reproducer: E7/E8: 60 wrong passwords in 4.5 s, all 401, no 429; 300 consecutive wrong TOTP guesses, zero 429; the same valid TOTP code accepted twice (`first -> HTTP 200, second use of same code -> HTTP 200`); with no limiter, a 6-digit code (3 valid values per 10^6 across the +-1 window) is brute-forceable online; unmeasured, only the absence of any throttle was reproduced (and F-REG-01 makes the second factor moot anyway).
impact: online password/TOTP guessing and credential stuffing; registration spam (open, unverified).
root_cause: absent middleware.
recommendation: fix - per-IP and per-account limiter with backoff, one-time TOTP counter storage.
regression_check: burst test expects 429; replay test expects 401.

title: No body-size limits and no server-side archive validation on publish
exploitability: any org owner/admin (publish); anonymous for JSON endpoints.
location: packages.go:111 (`ParseMultipartForm(32<<20)` is only the in-memory threshold, the comment says "32 MB max"), 169-200 (streams any bytes to disk, no size cap, no gzip/tar check); auth.go:39 etc. (`json.NewDecoder(r.Body)` unbounded); server.go:59-62
trigger_reproducer: E13: 200 MiB of non-archive bytes published as a version -> 201 (size 209,715,200 recorded), taking 2.5 s; 60 MiB JSON login body processed (401). Multipart spill also writes a temp copy in `$TMP`, doubling disk use. A client-side `Publish` buffers the full tarball in memory (client.go:148-159).
impact: disk exhaustion, memory pressure; registry can host arbitrary blobs; invalid archives are served to consumers who then hit F-REG-10.
root_cause: `ParseMultipartForm` misread as a limit; no validation stage.
recommendation: fix - `http.MaxBytesReader` (global and per route), validate the tarball with the hardened extractor before accepting, per-user quotas.
regression_check: oversize and non-tar uploads -> 413/400.

title: Sessions cannot be revoked; no purpose/typ on JWTs; 7-day lifetime

recommendation: refactor - server-side session table (or token-version column) checked in middleware; shorter TTL.
regression_check: logout/password-change invalidates old tokens.

title: Transport/browser hardening absent (no TLS, cookie not Secure, CORS `*`, no security headers)
exploitability: network attacker where deployed without a TLS terminator; any website for CORS (no credentials, so limited).

root_cause: server assumes a reverse proxy but nothing documents or enforces it.
recommendation: fix - document proxy requirement, add `Secure` when `base_url` is https, add headers + CSP, restrict CORS to configured origins.

title: Registry selection is nondeterministic and credentials are keyed by raw string (dependency-confusion exposure)
exploitability: user who has logged in to more than one registry (or two spellings of one).
location: internal/registry/credentials.go:259-268 (`DefaultRegistry` returns the first key of a Go map), :230-236 (exact-string key), client.go:31-43; used by `pull` (registry.go:187-196), `versions`, `token create`

recommendation: refactor - explicit `defaultRegistry` plus `scopes` mapping, normalised URL keys.
regression_check: multi-registry test with a fixed order.

title: Pull writes untrusted files into the project and can overwrite existing files; pulled `veld.config.json` can carry a hook
evidence_status: suspected risk (the write was reproduced via MITM; the hook executing was not run)

title: Position handling uses byte offsets with no positionEncoding negotiation
trigger_reproducer: pos.py — line `// <3 emoji> Local`, hover at UTF-16 column 11 returns null, at byte column 17 returns the model.
expected_vs_actual: expected UTF-16 code-unit columns (the LSP default), or an advertised `positionEncoding: utf-8`; actual raw byte indexing with nothing advertised. Slicing a multi-byte rune is also possible in completion (`line[:pos.Character]`).
impact: hover, completion and definition misbehave after any non-ASCII character on the line (comments, descriptions). Possible index slicing into the middle of a rune.
root_cause: string indexing by `Position.Character` without conversion.
recommendation: fix — convert UTF-16 columns to rune/byte offsets in one helper, or negotiate utf-8.
regression_check: unit test with emoji and accented characters before the cursor for hover, completion and definition.

title: Diagnostics are first-error-only, whole-line, and often on the wrong line
trigger_reproducer: `output: Unknwn` is reported on the `action A {` line (0-based 2 or 7), not on the token; range is `character 0..1000` always.
expected_vs_actual: expected a range over `Unknwn`; actual the whole line, 1000 characters wide, and only the first lex/parse error.
impact: squiggles cover entire lines (and line 1 on a message with no line), and a file with several errors shows one at a time.
root_cause: errors carry only a line number, which the server regex-extracts from `err.Error()`; the lexer tracks no columns.
recommendation: refactor — return structured errors (line, column, length) from the internal/errors package instead of parsing message text.
regression_check: golden test asserting range start/end for a type error and a syntax error.

title: Lexer silently accepts unterminated string literals (CLI too)

impact: typos in descriptions or import paths pass validation; with a missing closing quote on an import the wrong path is used.

recommendation: fix — return a lexer error when a string ends at newline/EOF.

title: JSON-RPC conformance defects (shutdown result, null diagnostics, exit code)

expected_vs_actual: expected `"result": null`, `"diagnostics": []`, and exit code 1 when exit arrives without shutdown.
impact: strict clients (and some Neovim/Emacs/Helix configs) can reject the response or treat `null` diagnostics as an error; shell supervisors see a clean exit after an unclean shutdown.
root_cause: `omitempty` on `Result` and a nil slice for no diagnostics; `os.Exit(0)`.
recommendation: fix — always emit `result` for successful replies, use empty slices, track the shutdown flag.
regression_check: transport test that checks the raw JSON for `"result":null` and `"diagnostics":[]`.

title: Single-threaded, un-debounced, no recover — slow parses block everything and a panic kills the server
location: internal/lsp/server.go:34-49; internal/lsp/handler.go (no recover anywhere in internal/lsp)
trigger_reproducer: 2.4 MB doc: each didChange costs about 744 ms, and a hover sent after it waited 684 ms. No panic was reproduced (garbage, deep nesting and empty inputs were all handled).
expected_vs_actual: expected cancellable/debounced work with panic isolation; actual serial full re-analysis per message.
impact: typing in a very large contract lags; any latent parser/validator panic terminates the editor's language service (the CLI binary exits) with no log.
root_cause: synchronous dispatch, no coalescing of changes, no `defer recover()`.
recommendation: fix — wrap dispatch in recover, debounce diagnostics per URI, and run requests off the read loop.
regression_check: test feeding an input known to panic (fuzz target) and asserting the server answers the next request.

title: `extends` validation misses field-override conflicts; cycle check is cubic

title: Credentials stored in plaintext; file permissions are not enforced on Windows
exploitability: local user/process with read access to the profile; backup tools.
trigger_reproducer: file content `{"registries":{"http://localhost:18080":{"token":"vtk_DYPN...","username":"cli5487"}}}`; `icacls` on Windows shows inherited ACEs for other principals (e.g. a sandbox user group) - mode bits are meaningless there. Write is not atomic (no temp+rename) and read-modify-write is unlocked (concurrent logins can lose entries). On Unix 0600 applies only on creation (an existing looser file keeps its mode).
impact: standard "plaintext dotfile" exposure; acceptable on Unix, weaker on Windows; no OS keychain integration; `VELD_TOKEN`-style env override does not exist for CI.
root_cause: simple file store.
recommendation: fix - keep file but chmod after write, atomic write, optional env token, consider keychain later.
regression_check: perms test on Unix.

recommendation: fix - explicit file list from the package manifest, `Lstat` and skip non-regular files, zero ModTime, check errors.
regression_check: pack test with symlink, nested and unreadable files.

title: Email handling: SMTP proceeds without TLS, verification never enforced, token logged, HTML injection
evidence_status: source-supported defect (SMTP not exercised; not configured)
exploitability: network attacker between server and SMTP host; log readers; any user (username in email).
location: email.go:97-106 (STARTTLS optional, then `loginAuth` has no TLS requirement: lines 33-35 vs stdlib PlainAuth), email.go:68 (To header from user input; `Rcpt` rejects CR/LF so injection is blocked in practice), auth.go:363 (full verify URL with token logged), auth.go:43-50 (email format unvalidated), email.go template `fmt.Sprintf` with raw username (HTML injection into the email), whole `email_verified` flag unused for authorization (REPRODUCED: unverified account publishes).
impact: SMTP credentials can be sent in cleartext after a stripped STARTTLS; account verification is cosmetic, so spam/squatting is unconstrained.
root_cause: copy-paste mail code, verification is not a gate.
recommendation: fix - require TLS before AUTH (or implicit TLS), strip tokens from logs, escape template values, gate publishing/org creation on `email_verified` when SMTP is configured.
regression_check: fake SMTP server that withholds STARTTLS.
